name: Put Ratio Spread 1x2 (Put Front Spread)
summary: Buy one nearer put and sell two further-OTM puts in the same expiry, usually for a credit; profits most if the underlying drifts down to the short strike, with large risk below it.

legs.strike_rule: Long put ATM or slightly ITM, 0.45-0.60 delta.
Two short puts at 0.20-0.30 delta, placed so the package opens for a net credit.

max_profit: (long strike - short strike) * 100 + net credit, at exactly the short strike at expiry
max_loss: Effectively undefined -- (short strike * 100) - max profit per unit, as the underlying falls toward zero. One short put is uncovered.
breakevens: lower breakeven: short strike - (max profit per share); if opened for a credit there is no upper breakeven

greeks.delta: slightly negative at entry, turning sharply positive as price falls toward the short strike

when_to_use: Expecting a controlled pullback into support with elevated IV. Equity put skew means the two short puts pay well, making credit entries easy -- which is precisely what makes this structure seductive and dangerous in a crash.
entry_rules: BLOCKED ON THIS ACCOUNT. One of the two short puts is uncovered -- Level 4 authority, which Alpaca does not offer; the MLeg engine rejects uncovered legs.
Defined-risk substitute: a put broken-wing butterfly (buy 1 higher put, sell 2 middle puts, buy 1 lower put) -- same profile with a hard floor, Level 3 legal.

If it were enabled: IV rank >= 40; net credit > $0.00; short strike at or below support tested twice in 60 sessions; DTE 30-45; lower breakeven at least 2.0 ATR(20) below spot (markets fall faster than they rise, so demand more room than the call version).
management_rules: If enabled: take profit at 50% of max profit or close for any credit once within 1% of the short strike.
Stop: close if the underlying trades below the lower breakeven, or if position delta reaches +0.50 per unit.
In a VIX spike above 30, close immediately regardless of P/L -- downside ratio spreads are the classic blow-up trade in a volatility event.
exit_rules: Flat by 15:45 ET on expiration day.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: assignment on both short puts delivers 200 long shares per unit against one long put; close before 15:30 ET on expiry day whenever the short puts are ITM.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: close whenever the short puts are ITM with extrinsic < $0.10 -- ITM puts are exercised early for carry.
assignment_risk: High. Two short puts, one covered. Double assignment means buying 200 shares per unit at the short strike, with only 100 shares' worth of long-put protection above.
buying_power: The covered pair holds the vertical width; the extra short put holds Reg-T naked put margin (or cash-secured value). Not available on Alpaca.
liquidity_needs: OI >= 500 both strikes; short leg quoted size >= 20.
common_mistakes: Selling downside ratio spreads into a rising-VIX tape; treating the credit as the edge; not stress-testing a -10% gap.
zero_dte_notes: Not permitted, and 0DTE downside gaps are exactly the scenario that destroys this structure.
family: Two-leg verticals and same-expiry two-leg combos (call/put verticals, straddles, strangles, guts, synthetics/risk reversals, ratio verticals and backspreads)
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
